title: At Stanford, Exploring Companionship Without Giving Up Control
summary: Chorong Park's invited talk and research conversations explored how companion robots can respect older adults' choices, preferences, and changing boundaries.

sources.label: Read Chorong Park's original LinkedIn post

paragraphs.text: Chorong Park brought ELARA's community-engaged research to the Stanford Robotics Center on October 12, 2026, for an invited talk, "When Robots Feel Like Companions: Designing Trust and Agency with Older Adults." The visit connected older adults' experiences with questions about how robots behave and how people understand them.

Park asked how a robot might support a meaningful relationship while leaving people free to question it, redirect it, or walk away. Her seminar connected emotional connection with privacy and autonomy. The practical design challenge is not simply making a robot feel friendly, but keeping its behavior understandable and its assistance optional.

In her October 21 reflection, Park described conversations about the developing Pupper collaboration and how robot personalities and interaction styles might fit older adults' preferences. Exchanges with Stanford researchers also explored how everyday needs could inform useful robot capabilities, rather than starting with technology and looking for a use afterward.

Park also reported visiting the Palo Alto VA Hospital Simulation Center and discussing potential collaborations around aging, cognitive health, and human-centered technology. These were exploratory conversations connecting design, engineering, and clinical perspectives, not announcements of completed studies or established health benefits.

review.notes: Complete owner-authored caption, profile and original activity permalink checked in the expanded connected feed and original LinkedIn post. Feed gives October 21, 2026 at 3:06 PM CDT; original post displays a 15-photo gallery. All 15 full-size images were opened in source order, downloaded without alteration, visually reviewed, and checked for dimensions and SHA-256. Original collages/composition retained; no thumbnails substituted and no identities inferred from photographs. Stanford Robotics Center's primary seminar listing independently confirms the October 12 event, exact title and autonomy/privacy focus. Additional visits and research conversations are attributed to Park; developing and potential collaborations are not presented as completed studies, formal institutional agreements or clinical benefits. Elphi slide imagery is identified as concept visualization. No confidential robot-accessory details included.
